newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cricket-Sohail suspended for one match for dissent.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cricket-Sohail suspended for one match for dissent.

text.p: Pakistan opener Aamir Sohail has been suspended for one match for dissent and will miss the opening match of the World Series limited overs final against West Indies, the Australian Cricket Board said on Friday.

Sohail was reported by match referee Raman Subba Row for his reaction after being dismissed during Pakistan's three-wicket defeat against Australia on Thursday, adding another entry to his disciplinary record.
Subba Row announced his decision after conducting a hearing into the incident at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
Pakistan will face West Indies in a best-of-three final, starting in Sydney on Saturday.

The left-handed batsman was clearly unhappy at the circumstances surrounding his dismissal for six and appeared to gesticulate towards umpires Darryl Hair and Peter Parker as he walked back to the pavilion.

Sohail hooked a short-pitched ball from fast bowler Anthony Stuart to give Darren Lehmann a simple catch at fine leg but it was apparent the opener believed the delivery should have been called a no-ball because it bounced above shoulder height.
Fourteen months ago, Subba Row fined Sohail half his match fee and handed him a two-match suspended sentence for throwing his bat during the second test against Australia in Hobart.
Sohail threw his bat to the ground as he walked back to the pavilion after being dismissed.
At the limited overs World Cup in Australia in 1992, Sohail was fined US$250 for misconduct after he disputed his dismissal against Australia in Perth.
